findings.location: design.md#Decision: The export loads every event, then writes the CSV
findings.recommendation: Cost grows linearly with the organization's history on a request path: at about 40 000 events per organization and per month kept seven years (design.md#Context), one export holds up to ~3.4 million rows in an array, then a second full copy as one CSV string, per concurrent request. Stream instead: read the rows with a server-side cursor or keyset batches (`WHERE org_id = $1 AND (created_at, id) > ($2, $3) ORDER BY created_at, id LIMIT n`), select only the exported columns rather than `*`, and write each batch to the response stream as it arrives. Keep the spec's result intact (every event, oldest first). Add a task for it, and a test with a large fixture checking memory stays bounded.
findings.title: The export loads an unbounded result set into memory

findings.location: design.md#Decision: The export loads every event, then writes the CSV
findings.recommendation: The service has "one event loop per instance" (design.md#Context): mapping and joining millions of rows in one synchronous call stalls every other request on that instance for the whole build, and its cost grows with the audit log. Format and write the CSV per batch (a Transform stream, or `res.write` per batch honouring backpressure via `drain`) so the loop yields between batches. Same streaming rework as R-performance-1, but a distinct defect: a cursor alone would still block if the string is built in one pass.
findings.title: Building the whole CSV synchronously blocks the event loop

findings.recommendation: The schema of `audit_events` is not in the repository, so the index could not be checked. Confirm an index on `(org_id, created_at)` exists (or add it in this change) and check the plan with `EXPLAIN`; without it each export scans and sorts the whole table across all organizations.

findings.recommendation: Record the streaming alternative and the expected volume (rows and bytes for a seven-year organization) in the decision, and back the choice with a measurement of memory and event-loop delay on a realistic export.
